toegepas.voor: Draai die aardbol na die Stille Oseaan.
toegepas.na: Draai die aardbol tot jy die Stille Oseaan sien.
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Draai die aardbol na' is an English-shaped instruction; turning until you see the ocean is the natural Afrikaans phrasing.
toegepas.fout: 'Draai die aardbol na die Stille Oseaan' is a loose instruction that can read as turning the globe in the ocean's direction.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Turning until you see the ocean is the natural, unambiguous Grade 4 phrasing and keeps the meaning.

toegepas.voor: kyk goed na wat om hom lê
toegepas.na: kyk goed na wat rondom dit lê
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'om hom' for a continent is colloquial and reads awkwardly; 'rondom dit' is clearer in written Afrikaans.
toegepas.fout: 'wat om hom lê' reads stiffly; 'om' alone is a weak way to say 'around' here.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'rondom dit' is clearer written Afrikaans for a Grade 4 reader and means the same thing.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: In standard written Afrikaans for learners an ocean is referred to as 'dit', not 'hy'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Hy' for a concrete noun such as an ocean is standard Afrikaans, so this is a lateral move.

na_skrywer.blok: Land en water op die aardbol
na_skrywer.voor: bedek saam die grootste deel van die aarde
na_skrywer.na: bedek saam die grootste deel van die aarde se oppervlak
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: The lesson uses the wording listed as NIE under BESKERM; the protected form says water covers most of the surface, not most of the earth.
na_skrywer.fout: The sentence uses the wording the protected list forbids: water covers most of the earth's surface, not most of the earth.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: A real fault, but adding 'se oppervlak' changes what the sentence claims, so the writer must make the fix using the protected wording.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

vlae.teks: Gebruik die rigtings om te sê waar die ander kontinente lê.
vlae.rede: 'die rigtings' is vague on its own; if an earlier lesson's term (e.g. compass directions) is meant, the writer should name it rather than a language agent guessing.
